reason: ATC J01CR and the AWaRe beta-lactam/inhibitor group put it with piperacillin-tazobactam. Kept apart because P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii are intrinsically resistant to it but not to piperacillin-tazobactam, and intrinsic resistance is stored per class.

ATC J01CR groups it with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid. Sulbactam itself is active against A. baumannii, so A. baumannii is not intrinsically resistant to this drug although it is to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid; a separate class keeps that difference.
ATC J01CR groups it with the aminopenicillin combinations. It has antipseudomonal activity that they lack, so it needs its own class for P. aeruginosa intrinsic resistance.
ATC files it under beta-lactamase inhibitors (J01CG). Its useful activity is limited to Acinetobacter, so it needs a class that the other four pathogens can be intrinsically resistant to.

ATC J01DD groups it with ceftriaxone and cefotaxime. P. aeruginosa is intrinsically resistant to ceftriaxone and cefotaxime but not to ceftazidime, and PDC (AmpC) overproduction affects ceftazidime specifically.
ATC files it under third-generation cephalosporins (J01DD). In that class, the ESBL and carbapenemase edges on cephalosporin-3rd-gen would wrongly exclude it. DECISIONS.md D6.

ATC files it under other cephalosporins (J01DI). Grouped with the other cephalosporin/inhibitor combination so that its inhibitor-specific failures are drug-level INACTIVATES rows rather than class edges.
ATC J01DI (other cephalosporins); AWaRe calls it fifth-generation. It binds PBP2a, so mecA must not exclude it while excluding every other cephalosporin.
ATC J01DI (other cephalosporins). It is stable to most carbapenemases including metallo-beta-lactamases, so no class-level carbapenemase edge applies to it, unlike other cephalosporins.
ATC J01DH groups it with meropenem and imipenem. P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii are intrinsically resistant to ertapenem only, so it needs its own class for intrinsic resistance.
ATC J01DH (carbapenems). Vaborbactam restores activity against KPC, so the class-level KPC edge on carbapenem must not apply; inhibitor-specific failures (MBLs, OXA-48-like) are drug-level rows.
ATC J01DH (carbapenems). Relebactam restores activity against KPC, so the class-level KPC edge on carbapenem must not apply; inhibitor-specific failures (MBLs, OXA-48-like) are drug-level rows.
ATC J01DF (monobactams). Avibactam protects aztreonam from serine beta-lactamases (ESBL, AmpC, KPC, OXA-48-like), so the class-level edges on monobactam must not exclude it.
